the spontaneous attributions of parents about their children with behavioural problems are associated with child callous unemotionality, but not parental mental health.

the spontaneous speech of parents of children with disruptive behavioural problems contains a wealth of information about the causal attributions they make about their children's behaviour and that this speech is associated with both child and parent characteristics.

the PASS is a reliable and valid tool for measuring parents' spontaneous causal attributions, that parents of children with emotional and behavioral problems make more positive than negative, and dispositional attributions about their referred child, and that parents' spontaneous attributions are associated with child factors, but not with parents' own mental heath.

the PASS coding system is a valid and reliable tool to assess parental spontaneous attributions about children with emotional and behavioral problems, and that these attributions are associated with child callous unemotionality and not with parental mental health problems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
parental attributions are associated with children's callous unemotioal traits, but that parental attributions do not seem to be related to parental psychopathology.
parents' spontaneous causal attributions are important in understanding the development and maintenance of child conduct problems, and should be taken into account in treatment planning.

parents of children with emotional and behavioral problems are able to make attributions that are associated with their child's callous unemtional traits and that these attributions may be a good target for intervention.
The main takeaway from our work is that
spontaneous parental speech about their children is rich and informative, and that it can be used in research and practice to better inform the design and delivery of parenting programmes.
parents' spontaneous attributions about their problem children are a rich source of information about the parent child relationship and child characteristics.
the quality of parental causal attributions is not a direct function of parental psychopathology, but rather of child factors.
